The deadline's Nov. 22. Williams Lake residents have until Sunday, Nov. 22 to drop off gift-filled shoeboxes at Evangelical Free Church for this year’s Operation Christmas Child drive. Kathy Shetler, a Williams Lake volunteer with Operation Christmas Child, has been involved since the mid 1990s when she began packing shoeboxes at Maranatha Christian School in Williams Lake. Operation Christmas Child is a Samaritan’s Purse project that works with local churches and ministries overseas to distribute gift-filled shoeboxes to children at Christian outreach events. Shetler suggested packing school supplies, hygiene items, a toy or craft kit and something to wear, such as a hat or gloves. Donors can choose to pack for a child ages two to four, five to nine or 10 to 14. Shetler asked donors to leave out candy, liquids, toothpaste, soap, glass items and war-themed toys. Shetler thanked Williams Lake residents for their generosity over the years. “It’s such an expression of love and compassion to children around the world that do not have much,” she said. Empty shoeboxes and brochures are available at the Evangelical Free Church, 1100 North 11th Ave., and at Kit and Kaboodle, 83A Second Ave. S. Filled shoeboxes can be dropped off at the church through Sunday, Nov. 22. Shetler said the boxes will travel through Kamloops to Calgary, where they’ll be checked before being shipped overseas.

Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson says there will be no fall legislative session as the new Conservative government gets its bearings in the short window between being sworn in and the holiday season. “Our government has an ambitious agenda, and we want to ensure legislation is properly prepared and receives the debate and consideration it deserves,” Doerkson said in a written statement on Monday (Nov. 16). The B.C. Conservative Party will have a large majority in the legislature when it does convene, after the party won 64 of 93 seats in the Oct. 24 election. This could include changes to the Massey Tunnel project. Doerkson has promised to scrap the tunnel and build a bridge instead. The new government could also get started building other infrastructure, like the promised urgent care centres and Surrey women’s and children’s hospital. items.title: [cbc.ca] Alberta bill sets data-centre limits and well cleanup funds
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Alberta introduced Bill 42 on Nov. 18, proposing new siting and water rules for large data centres and mandatory cleanup funding for every new oil and gas well. Centres using at least 10 megawatts would generally have to be at least 600 metres from homes and avoid top-quality or irrigated farmland; they would also face a near-zero cooling-water standard. The Alberta Utilities Commission would regulate the larger facilities. The province says about 30% of current proposals could be affected, while projects already far along in approvals or construction would be exempt. For new wells, companies would pay up to $50,000 initially and make equal annual payments for up to 10 years. The money would remain attached to the well if ownership changes. If a well becomes orphaned, its funding would go to the Orphan Well Association. The requirements are expected to cover wells drilled after April 1, 2027. The bill would also eliminate Alberta’s oil-sands emissions cap, which the province says is redundant with industrial carbon pricing.

More than 65 protests took place across Canada on Nov. 12 against Bill C-39, the federal Building Canada Strong Act, which would let Cabinet designate regions of “national interest” and accelerate approvals for major projects. Governments and regulators are reassessing privacy safeguards, with Finland reviewing rules governing workplace communications, Hong Kong launching a support program for organisations adopting artificial intelligence, and European lawmakers debating proposed changes to data-protection law. Finland is seeking views before deciding whether to pursue legislation, Hong Kong is offering training and surveying business practices, and European Union lawmakers and privacy specialists are disputing whether proposed simplifications would weaken protections. Finland’s Communications Ministry says national rules extend beyond the EU ePrivacy directive and have become harder to apply alongside newer laws. Hong Kong’s first initiative will offer three free data-security seminars for small businesses and NGOs; its AI and Data Privacy Survey 2026 is expected later this year.

items.content_html:

An exposed database at the Latvian branch of telecommunications provider CSCTelecom contained more than 125 million text messages sent from October 2022 through September 2026, Cybernews researchers reported. The messages were sent for banks, retailers, medical providers, airBaltic and Latvia’s emergency number 112. The database updated in real time and included phone numbers, full message contents and metadata; some texts contained bank balances and transactions, medical information, travel details, authentication codes and password-reset links. The exposure extended to businesses and users in Lithuania and Estonia. Researchers found the database on Sept. 28, and it was no longer publicly accessible by Oct. 27. They have reported no evidence that malicious actors accessed it, but cybersecurity expert Kirils Solovjovs said it remains unclear whether anyone copied the data. Swedbank has stopped using CSCTelecom while the bank investigates; SEB said it used the provider only for limited pension-fund marketing messages and that sensitive customer information and funds were not affected. Latvia’s cyber incident response organization CERT.LV requested an in-depth investigation by the company and referred the matter to law enforcement.

France raised its bird flu risk classification for the mainland from moderate to high, the highest of three alert levels, effective Nov. 20. The order requires poultry to be kept indoors or otherwise protected from wild birds, with some exceptions allowing smaller or adapted outdoor areas. Authorities also tightened rules on poultry gatherings and certain bird movements. The Agriculture Ministry cited three confirmed outbreaks in backyard flocks since late October, infections among wild birds in France and rising cases along migration routes in neighboring countries. Officials fear the virus could spread from wild birds to commercial farms. France raised the alert from negligible to moderate earlier in November. The latest order follows detections in 24 European countries since Aug. 1, according to the animal-health surveillance bulletin.

items.title: [proplanta.de] EU convenes crisis talks as freezer hacks spread to Germany, Romania
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

The European Commission convened two crisis meetings after cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems spread across Europe, with incidents reported in at least 11 countries, including Germany and Romania. The attacks remotely raised temperatures or triggered defrost cycles, forcing retailers to discard food; no group has claimed responsibility, and authorities have not established whether the incidents share a perpetrator. The wave follows a similar attack on French supermarkets in October. A store in Lilienthal, Germany, said it had to discard goods worth more than €360,000, while six Romanian stores were affected. Italy’s government held talks with intelligence and cybersecurity officials and said the impact there was limited to a small number of commercial sites; it reported no health risk from thawed food. EU officials are coordinating with national authorities, who are conducting the investigations. Agriculture Commissioner Christophe Hansen said the bloc’s food supply was not currently threatened, and the Commission said the incidents showed a need for stronger cybersecurity across the EU.

The Internal Revenue Service raised federal income tax bracket thresholds for 2027, allowing taxpayers to earn more before entering a higher bracket. Tax rates remain unchanged, with the top rate still 37%. For single filers, the 22% bracket starts above $52,025 and the 37% bracket above $661,375; for married couples filing jointly, those thresholds are $104,050 and $793,650. The IRS also increased the maximum child tax credit to $2,300, including a refundable portion of up to $1,800, and raised the maximum earned income tax credit for qualifying families with at least three children to $8,496. The annual inflation adjustments are intended to keep wage increases from pushing taxpayers into higher brackets when their purchasing power has not increased.

items.title: [news.un.org] UN warns 2026 heat records signal accelerating climate extremes
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Earth’s energy imbalance has reached its highest level since monitoring began, and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) says 2026 is on track to rank among the four warmest years on record. Global surface temperature averaged about 1.47°C above the preindustrial level from January through September; a developing, unusually strong El Niño could push the annual figure higher and prolong extreme heat into 2027. The agency released its report as the U.N. climate summit COP31 opened in Antalya, Turkey, with negotiations scheduled through Nov. 20. The agency says each of the past 12 years ranked among the 12 warmest on record, with 2023-2026 likely to be the four warmest years. Greenhouse gases from human activity are trapping heat; the ocean absorbs about 90% of the excess, while sea levels and ocean temperatures have reached records. The WMO warns that the accumulating heat will intensify heat waves, droughts, tropical cyclones and heavy rain. A separate U.N. Environment Programme assessment says warming will exceed 1.5°C under every plausible emissions pathway. Returning below that threshold this century would require near-zero emissions and the removal of hundreds of billions of tonnes of carbon dioxide. The WMO’s full 2026 climate report is due in March 2027.

items.content_html:

MIT researchers found that older adults had significantly weaker waves of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), which helps clear waste from the brain during sleep, than younger adults. The researchers used brain imaging and electroencephalography to study volunteers ages 18 to 39 and 60 to 84, linking the reduced flow partly to weaker deep-sleep brain waves and diminished vascular responses. Separately, a study described in a paper shared on Reddit found that LSD-related gene-expression patterns in rats and mice ran counter to some patterns associated with human brain aging. LSD also reduced certain amyloid-beta-related changes in mouse brain-cell cultures. These are preclinical findings, not evidence that LSD prevents dementia in people.

items.content_html:

About 20 Indigenous Awá living in isolation approached the Guajajara village of Tawari on Monday, November 16, in Arariboia Indigenous Territory, in the Brazilian state of Maranhão; they received yams and returned to the forest. Members of the Guajajara community recorded the encounter, and the organization Survival International shared the footage. The National Foundation for Indigenous Peoples (Funai) and Indigenous health personnel are in the area. The government activated an emergency coordination mechanism to assess the situation and health risks. Authorities said they are still assessing the initial information and that this isolated approach does not mean the Awá have abandoned their isolation. The reason for the visit has not been confirmed; Survival International linked it to pressure from illegal loggers, hunters, and ranchers on the territory. Local residents voiced concern about the thinness of some children and older people. There is also concern about the risk of infections, given the group’s limited exposure to common pathogens.

items.title: [scientificamerican.com] Neanderthal DNA variant linked to smaller visual brain region, lower schizophrenia odds
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Researchers report that a Neanderthal-derived DNA variant is associated with a smaller occipital lobe and lower odds of schizophrenia in modern humans. In UK Biobank data, each copy of the variant corresponded to about 0.85 cubic centimeters less occipital-lobe volume; people with two copies had nearly 10% lower odds of schizophrenia than those with no copies. The occipital lobe processes visual information. The variant lies near DAAM1, a gene involved in brain development, but researchers have not established how it affects the brain or whether the smaller lobe explains the schizophrenia association. The variant was not associated with a meaningful difference in intelligence, and outside researchers cautioned against drawing conclusions about Neanderthal brain function from the findings in modern humans. The study was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Its authors say further work, including studies using brain organoids or animal models, could investigate the mechanism.
